transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-01-09
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-2028-01-09-ravenbrook-01 (placeholder)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Oliver (Ravenbrook Head of Search), Tasha (ML Eng), Noah (CTO), Priya (Product)

Summary:
Quick Hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings endpoint + 2-step reranker pattern. Demoed Redwood Console trace for per-route latency, Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, discussed SOC2/KMS questions and pilot/bench plan. Agreed to trial and benchmarking session.

Topics covered:
- embeddings: dimensionality, storage, vector DB integration
- reranker endpoint: API params, candidate scoring, contextualization
- hosted API vs dedicated (latency/cost tradeoffs)
- Optimize suggestions: auto-batching, quant profiles, KV cache
- security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to run through the hosted API flow today, specifically the embeddings plus a small reranker demo. i think we'll aim for a hands-on demo and leave time for questions at the end.
[00:18] Oliver (Ravenbrook): great, thanks, we're trying to understand how this fits into our current stack — we use Postgres + a vector index for candidate retrieval and then a small transformer re-ranker in an inference service. primary concerns are latency at 99th percentile and cost at scale.
[00:37] Luca (Redwood): sounds good. quick intro: i'll show the API call patterns, the embeddings route and then the reranker endpoint which is optimized for scoring candidates — it's a hosted two-step flow so you can keep retrieval in your vector DB and call Redwood to re-score.
[00:52] Tasha (Ravenbrook): a quick note: our queries are short, avg 12 tokens, but we occasionally have longer context concat from user profile, up to 200 tokens. we need to know token pricing and token latency.
[01:12] Samir (Redwood): right, and we have a few levers — batching, prefix KV cache, and quantization recommendations via Optimize. for short queries you get lower token cost but the per-request overhead can dominate, so we usually suggest small batching or enabling continuous batching in our hosted api.
[01:35] Speaker 1 (transcript artifact): um-huh mm.
[01:40] Luca (Redwood): i'll share the console now, bear with me while i switch screens. (pause) ok, console -> projects -> ravenbrook-demo. here you can see per-route latency histogram, token cost breakdown, and a live request trace that includes the reranker call.
[02:05] Oliver: can you point out where the embeddings dimension and model are set?
[02:10] Luca: sure — on the embeddings call we pick model=open-emb-2048 (demo model), dimension=1024 in this demo. you can change that via the SDK or REST param. we also show model performance profiles so you can compare latency and cost across options.
[02:29] Tasha: do you do any on-the-fly dimensionality reduction? we currently do PCA down to 256 for storage savings.
[02:36] Luca: we don't do automatic PCA; Optimize can recommend lower-dimension model variants or quantized variants if accuracy is acceptable. for storage we recommend quantized float16 or int8 variants and we have a guide in the docs.
[02:50] Maya: quick architecture recap — retrieval in your vector DB returns top-N candidates, then you call our reranker endpoint with the query + candidate contexts. our reranker supports batched candidate scoring, per-candidate metadata, and returns scores + optional rationales.
[03:10] Noah: how are tokens counted when you send the candidate contexts? is it per-request token billing plus embedding costs?
[03:18] Samir: good question — embeddings are charged per embedding call separately; the reranker scoring is billed per token for the model used. we show token-level breakdown in the console so you can map cost to each route.
[03:34] Priya: any recommended top-N for candidate retrieval? we currently return 50 and then re-rank — that's maybe too many.
[03:41] Luca: 50 is common, but for latency-sensitive flows we recommend 10–20 and then tune. you can also do a first-pass cheap filter with approximate scores, then call the reranker on the top 10. caching also helps, e.g., prefix cache for repeated queries.
[03:58] Oliver: show us a live call?
[04:01] Luca: yep, i'll run a quick notebook demo — curl examples first for the embeddings endpoint, then reranker.
[04:08] (keyboard sounds)
[04:13] Luca: example curl: POST /v1/embeddings with model=open-emb-2048 body {"input": "how do i reset my router"} returns a 1024-d vector. then we store that vector in your vector index. next our search pipeline returns candidate ids and we call POST /v1/reranker with model=re-rank-1 and payload {"query":"how do i reset my router","candidates":[{ "id":1,"text":"..." }, ...] }. response includes scores and the top recommendation.
[04:46] Tasha: is there an option to return token-level attention or saliency so we can debug relevance regressions?
[04:52] Samir: we can return per-candidate rationales of a few tokens (structured) but not full attention maps. we also surface evaluation diffs in Optimize tied to your eval set so you can see quality regressions over time.
[05:07] Oliver: can we store embeddings in our S3 bucket and have Redwood pull them?
[05:13] Maya: there are two routes — you can store embeddings wherever and call the embeddings endpoint to compute on demand, or you can upload precomputed vectors to your vector DB. Redwood's private deployments can integrate with customer S3 for on-prem/air-gapped setups, but hosted customers typically manage vectors with their chosen index (e.g., Pinecone or Faiss).
[05:35] Speaker 2 (microphone glitch): sorry background noise.
[05:40] Luca: back to the reranker: i'll show a trace — this is a single request that scored 12 candidates. trace shows network time, model latency, and the KV cache hit at prefix level. notice the 95th pct is around 220ms in this demo region; with a dedicated setup that can drop to ~120ms.
[06:05] Oliver: that 220ms includes our network to Redwood?
[06:09] Luca: it's server-side only; client to us depends on region and route. we recommend pinning region to reduce RTT or use our dedicated private deployment in your VPC for consistent low latency.
[06:21] Tasha: about Optimize suggestions you mentioned — can it tune batching automatically?
[06:26] Samir: yes, Optimize runs offline analysis on your request pattern and suggests batching settings and queue sizes. it will also flag quality changes if you enable evals. it's conservative by default and you can accept suggestions in the console.
[06:40] Priya: do you support function/tool calls or structured output in reranker?
[06:46] Luca: structured output is supported as JSON schema responses; tool calling is more in the generation endpoint but you can include tool metadata per candidate for downstream processing.
[06:57] Oliver: security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS — how do these work for hosted?
[07:02] Maya: hosted customers get SOC2 Type II, full audit logs surfaced in the Console. SSO via SAML/OIDC for the console, RBAC for team roles, and for encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; hosted supports encryption at rest with our managed keys and can support BYOK for enterprise contracts.
[07:26] Noah: would BYOK be an option for hosted or only Private?
[07:30] Maya: currently BYOK is offered as part of the enterprise hosted contract (not default), and full HSM/BYOK is part of the Private on-prem package. we'll include the security pack in the follow-up.
[07:44] Tasha: for compliance we also need data residency options — can you guarantee region-specific storage for embeddings?
[07:51] Samir: yes, we can filter which region stores embeddings; for strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated or Private. hosted has region selections but not hard physical separation by default.
[08:05] Oliver: what's the expected lift to integrate our existing retrieval pipeline?
[08:09] Luca: low — typical integration is: 1) compute or reuse existing embeddings -> store in vector DB; 2) add candidate retrieval call in your search service; 3) call Redwood reranker with candidate contexts. SDKs have helpers and we have a step-by-step repo. estimate 2–4 dev days to get an end-to-end pilot.
[08:26] Priya: can Redwood handle multi-lingual embeddings? we have Spanish+English corpora.
[08:31] Samir: yes models support multi-lingual embeddings and Optimize will surface if a different model is better per language.
[08:41] Maya: small tangent — cost calculation. for demo we toggled a model profile that is more accurate but more expensive. we showed cost per 1k requests in the console example.
[08:54] Oliver: do you have guidance on A/B testing reranker variants?
[08:58] Luca: yes — Console supports rollout policies: canary, percentage, and A/B with automatic fallback. you can route a percentage of reranker traffic to a new model and compare metrics (latency, click-through, precision on your eval set).
[09:14] (screen share: Optimize page)
[09:17] Samir: here's an Optimize suggestion: for your query distribution (short queries 70%), it suggests enabling continuous batching window 50ms and quantizing to int8 for the reranker in non-prod. expected cost reduction ~27% with <1% quality delta on the eval.
[09:38] Tasha: can we run local perf tests? we prefer to run a bench with our dataset and the same env.
[09:43] Luca: absolutely — we'll set up a dedicated trial project with a known quota and provide a benchmarking harness (JMeter/curl scripts and sample notebook). that's part of the trial onboarding.
[09:56] Oliver: procurement questions: what does SLA look like for hosted?
[10:01] Maya: hosted has tiered SLAs — standard (best-effort), enterprise hosted has 99.9% uptime SLA and dedicated capacity options for higher guarantees. Private has contractual SLA with on-prem support. we'll include an SLA excerpt in the follow-up.
[10:18] Priya: any known degradation modes? for instance when model falls back due to capacity.
[10:24] Samir: yes — we have automated fallback policies: model variant fallback (smaller model), region fallback, and queued backpressure. Console will show fallbacks in traces and optimize suggests alternate configs.
[10:40] Tasha: does the reranker produce deterministic scores? we saw nondeterminism previously in other systems which made A/B analysis tricky.
[10:47] Luca: scores are deterministic per model version if you fix model seed and config; for stochastic models we expose the config and you can pin seed. we recommend version pinning in production.
[10:58] Oliver: ok let's talk pricing ballpark — for 200k qps monthly what numbers should we expect?
[11:04] Maya: rough ballpark: embeddings cost per compute call + reranker token cost. i'll capture exact numbers and present a scenario: default model vs quantized model. we'll send a cost model spreadsheet.
[11:15] (questions from audience)
[11:20] Noah: latency requirements for search are 150ms p95 ideally, can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[11:27] Luca: on shared hosted, p95 around 200–300ms depending on region, but we can get to ~120ms p95 on Dedicated in the same region and ~80–100ms p95 for private infra tuned for the workload.
[11:45] Tasha: do you provide prebuilt retriever connectors?
[11:48] Samir: we have examples for Pinecone, Milvus, and Faiss and a small SDK that wraps candidate fetch + reranker call. we'll share the SDK link.
[12:00] (demo continues with live curl responses and small typo in logs 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache')
[12:25] Luca: that was a typo in the logs, kv cash, uh we mean kv cache.
[12:31] Priya: ha noted.
[12:35] Maya: quick recap before Q&A: 1) embeddings endpoint is configurable, store vectors wherever, 2) reranker endpoint is optimized for candidate scoring and supports batching + rationales, 3) Console + Optimize help tune cost/latency and monitor regressions, 4) security pack + trial to follow.
[12:58] Oliver: ok final ask — can we get a two-week trial with quotas to run our bench and an SLA excerpt + security docs?
[13:07] Maya: yes, we'll send security docs and spin up a trial. Luca will own the trial onboarding and Samir will attach Optimize suggestions and the bench harness.
[13:21] (closing remarks)
[13:25] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes, docs, and next steps.
[13:30] Noah: thanks all.
[13:33] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels like Speaker 1/2, small transcription errors (kv cash), timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
